studies.task: Write an advertising proposal of 200 + words for an iPhone Leather Flip Case during a 20-minute task divided into 10-minute idea generation and idea elaboration phases (PDF p. 14, Appendix G).

preregistration.where: AsPredicted, https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf (PDF p. 7, Section 6.1). The protocol is not included in the PDF; direct urllib retrieval was blocked by network permissions.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Novelty is innovation and uniqueness of the proposal and advertising copy. Consensual assessment by marketing experts using the same approach as Study 2 (PDF p. 7, Section 6.2). Study 2 describes seven-point scales, three marketing experts blind to purpose, hypotheses and condition, and averaging their scores for each participant (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 5.1.2). The number of raters is not restated for Study 3; the exact proposal version scored is not identified.

estimates.control_arm: GenAI in idea elaboration phase, high perceived intelligence and GenAI in idea elaboration phase, low perceived intelligence (combined)

paper_effect.standardizer: Point-biserial correlation with the randomized collaboration-phase dummy CP; no SD-based mean-difference standardizer is stated. Section 6.3.1 codes 1 = idea elaboration phase and 0 = idea generation phase.

estimates.notes: The printed correlation is negative because CP codes elaboration as one. It therefore favors generation, the named treatment arm. The correlation retains its printed sign and is oriented opposite to treatment minus control; downstream code must account for that coding before interpreting direction. The novelty mediation analysis uses the opposite phase coding, but it is not the source of this estimate. This is the unadjusted, full-sample correlation of randomized phase with the participant-level outcome, pooling high and low perceived-intelligence cells within each phase. The M and SD in the quoted table row summarize all conditions together; they are not treatment or control means or SDs. No arm sizes, arm-level outcome summaries, raw phase difference, or total-contrast SE/CI/test statistic are printed. The reported significance bound is based on participant scores; rater agreement statistics and mediation uncertainty are not uncertainty for this contrast. AI collaboration occurred during the assigned phase of the same creative task, so the question remains with_ai. outcome_with_ai is null because access in the non-assigned phase and the exact submission rated are not reported (PDF p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; PDF p. 14, Appendices G-H).

not_extracted.what: S4 / Study 3: novelty/usefulness correlations with measured covariates, mediators, and each other
not_extracted.reason: These correlations do not contrast randomized AI configurations. Only the CP column represents the full-sample randomized collaboration-phase comparison (PDF p. 8, Table 3). In particular, outcome correlations with PGenAII do not identify the high-versus-low randomized intelligence manipulation.

open_items: Study 3 does not print randomized counts, factorial cell sizes, or analyzed counts by phase. The recruited count is not explicitly an assignment count; no counts were inferred from the rounded phase-dummy mean or test degrees of freedom (PDF pp. 7-8).

Study 3 does not print arm-level novelty/usefulness means or SDs, raw total phase differences, or SEs/CIs for the total phase contrasts. Table 3 supplies only all-condition descriptive statistics and the phase-outcome correlations. Mediation uncertainty must not be substituted (PDF pp. 8-9).

For novelty, the printed r uses elaboration as one and generation as zero, opposite to the named generation-versus-elaboration treatment orientation. The original sign is preserved; downstream direction handling must use this local Table 3 coding. Hypothesis 3 uses a different phase coding (PDF p. 8).

The precise proposal version rated and ChatGPT access in the non-assigned phase are not stated; outcome_with_ai remains null while question is with_ai for collaboration within the same creative task (PDF p. 7, Sections 6.1-6.2; PDF p. 14, Appendices G-H).

The external preregistration is absent from the supplied PDF. Direct urllib requests to https://aspredicted.org/2hsq-9sg4.pdf and the named ScienceDirect article page were both blocked by socket permissions (WinError 10013). Preregistered primary-outcome status cannot be confirmed.

ChatGPT is named, but its underlying model/version and the experiment date are not specified. The AI-tool year is the product release year explicitly stated in the introduction, not an inferred study-model year (PDF pp. 1 and 7).

No full-sample novelty/usefulness contrast of randomized high versus low perceived intelligence is printed. Table 3 PGenAII is a measured scale; factorial cell summaries or analysis outputs would be needed (PDF pp. 7-9).
notes: Independent extraction B, 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion, including all appendices and references, was read. PDF tables, figures, methods and appendices were inspected; every retained numeric statistic and source quote was checked against pymupdf text. Screening study IDs are retained, so the sole eligible experiment is S4. The smaller laboratory experiments are separate samples and are not combined to meet the eligibility threshold. Figure 1 is conceptual; Figure 2 concerns self-reported cognitive overload. No effect sizes, counts, differences, standard errors or confidence intervals were calculated. Printed precision is retained in verbatim source quotes. The exact country and preregistered primary outcome remain unconfirmed.
